newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan plant makers see half-year profits tumble.
newsitem.headline: Japan plant makers see half-year profits tumble.

text.p: Major Japanese plant engineering company Chiyoda Corp announced a half-year loss on Friday and responded by saying it will try to turn things around under a new president.
Chiyoda's main rival Toyo Engineering Corp also said its profits plunged in the six months to September 30.
Chiyoda said it suffered a parent current loss of 14.68 billion yen ($132 million) in the half year, against profit of 2.59 billion yen ($23.3 million) in the same period a year ago.
It expects a full-year parent current loss of 24.0 billion yen ($216 million), against a profit of 4.61 billion yen ($41.5 million) in 1995/96.
Current profit is pre-tax profit and includes gains and losses made on securities investments and other non-operating activities.
The latest forecast is far worse than the company's September estimate of a loss of 17 billion yen ($153 million) for the business year.
Chiyoda said its president Masaaki Kashiwara would resign and vice president Masato Kitagawa would take the post on December 1.
"In order to refresh management following the poor earnings in the half-year period, we decided to change presidents," a Chiyoda spokesman said.

Meanwhile, rival Toyo Engineering's first-half parent current profit was down 70.6 percent year-on-year to 591 million yen ($5.32 million). Toyo said its full-year parent current profit would be 1.0 billion yen ($9.0 million), down from 3.55 billion yen ($31.9 million) a year ago.
The two companies build various plants, such as petroleum, chemical, electric power and gas plants.
The profitability of their projects worsened due to excessive competition and delays in finishing overseas projects, industry analysts said. ($1=111 yen)
